draft.title: The Armistice
card: An armistice is an agreement to stop fighting. It is not a peace treaty, which settles the terms of peace afterwards.
By late 1918 Germany's allies were collapsing. Its army had also been pushed back by Allied attacks on the Western Front.
Germany agreed to the Armistice. Fighting on the Western Front stopped at 11 am on 11 November 1918.
Australian soldiers were among the Allied troops who fought in the final months. For them, as for others, the war's fighting ended with the Armistice.
draft.remember: The Armistice ended the fighting, after Germany lost its allies and ground, but it was not a peace treaty.

a.q: Why did Germany agree to the Armistice in 1918?
opts: Its allies were collapsing and its army was pushed back
Its army had reached Paris and wanted to negotiate
Its government had signed a peace treaty with Russia
The Allies had stopped fighting and asked for talks
a.why: By late 1918 Germany's allies were collapsing and the Allies had pushed its army back, so it agreed to stop fighting. Reaching Paris is wrong because Germany was losing ground, not gaining it.
a.clue: Think about Germany's allies and where its army stood.

b.q: Mia reads that the Armistice was signed on 11 November 1918. What did it do?
opts: It stopped the fighting, but did not settle the peace terms
It settled the peace terms and ended the war in law
It stopped the fighting only for the Australian troops
It started the evacuation of troops from Gallipoli
b.why: An armistice is an agreement to stop fighting. A peace treaty is different, as it settles the terms of peace afterwards, so the second option is tempting but wrong.
b.clue: An armistice and a peace treaty are not the same thing.

a.best: Its allies were collapsing and its army was pushed back

b.best: It stopped the fighting, but did not settle the peace terms

problems.detail: 'For them, as for others, the war's fighting ended with the Armistice' is misleading. The Australian Corps was withdrawn from the Western Front line in early October 1918, after Montbrehain, so its fighting ended before 11 November. The Light Horse in the Middle East stopped fighting under the separate Armistice of Mudros with the Ottoman Empire, at the end of October 1918.

Why (b) calls 'the second option' the tempting wrong answer, but the options are shown in random order. Here the second option is the 'only for the Australian troops' one, while the tempting option is 'It settled the peace terms and ended the war in law'. The why should name the option by its content, not its position.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer. The card suggests Australians' fighting ended with the 11 November Armistice, but Australian infantry left the line in early October and the Light Horse stopped under the Ottoman armistice. Why (b) also refers to 'the second option', which does not work when the options are shuffled.
